source.name: USGS Copperwood Western Syncline drill-core geochemistry
source.license: CC0 1.0 Universal, as marked by the USGS release; retain attribution and source qualifications.
source.positionalAccuracy: WGS84 sample-site coordinates. USGS metadata reports no formal positional accuracy tests; borehole trajectories are not supplied.
source.depthInterpretation: Source reports interval depths from the surface in feet. Axis is not established as vertical. No vertical-depth or 3D trajectory reconstruction is made.
source.selection: Selected drill-core samples from a known copper deposit; not representative global exploration negatives or an independent test of the soil model.

source.name: USGS Slab2 — March 2018 archive
source.author: Gavin Hayes / U.S. Geological Survey
source.license: CC0 1.0 Universal; metadata use constraints: none
source.updateFrequency: None planned in this release metadata
source.depthConvention: Negated source depth grid z, following the supplied USGS query script; supplementary CSV depths retain their source sign. Units: km.
source.coordinates: Geographic longitude/latitude in degrees. Source grids use 0–360 longitude. A named horizontal/vertical datum is not declared in the supplied grid metadata.
source.uncertainty: Source depth uncertainty (PDF standard deviation, km); not a calibrated Baryon prediction interval or total uncertainty.
source.normalization: Every fifth index in both axes is retained for the grid preview (0.1 or 0.25 degrees according to actual grid spacing). All supplementary nodes are retained. Coordinates rounded to 6 decimals; grid attributes to 0.001 km/degrees. Missing cells remain absent; no interpolation or averaging.
metadataWarnings: README spacing differs from five actual grids.
The parent metadata lineage cites an apparently unrelated 2017 paper; the Slab2 publication is linked separately.
The archive README includes a placeholder DOI; the verified catalog DOI is retained.

structure.scope: Subducted slab geometry in 27 model regions. No global crustal composition, mineral inventory, borehole trajectory or ore-body model is inferred. External model ingestion is not new measured evidence or demonstrated Baryon model improvement.

source.name: USGS preliminary three-layer geologic model, version 1.1
source.authors: Sweetkind, Zellman and Goldberg / U.S. Geological Survey
source.license: CC0 1.0 Universal; acknowledge USGS and U.S. Bureau of Reclamation.
source.updateFrequency: As needed in source metadata; no fixed refresh interval.
source.verticalDatum: NAVD 88, as stated in USGS Data Report 1220; no vertical transformation applied by Baryon.
source.units: Altitudes in meters above the reported vertical datum. Derived depths are differences between cell-average altitudes.
source.accuracy: No formal horizontal, vertical or attribute accuracy assessment. Intended regional scale 1:2,500,000; data are not resolvable finer than 2.5-km cells.
warnings: Bedrock and basement have different geological meanings across regions; inspect the cell definition.
Null bedrock with BEDRX5 denotes an absent stratified bedrock unit; other nulls remain missing.
Some source notes describe manually adjusted or arbitrary altitudes; preserve them as modeled assumptions.
The report describes unsmoothed source boundaries and known regional inconsistencies. The XML also records some manual boundary adjustments.
One empty-geometry source row is retained outside the map.
Cell land-source key DAS1 is retained; the source table spells this entry DAS01. The explicit zero-padding alias is disclosed.

grid.transform: Inverse of Conus Albers + NAD83 to WGS 84 (1) (with axis order normalized for visualization)
grid.coordinateMethod: Center of each verified square cell, transformed for display. Altitudes remain cell averages, not site measurements.

glossary.Definition: Continental craton: basement surface is top of crystalline Precambrian rocks. Also includes Late Proterozoic sedimentary rocks in Minnesota and the Uinta Group
Perimeter of Gulf basin: basement surface is the base of the post-rift Jurassic-Cretaceous rocks
Atlantic Coastal Plain: basement surface is base of post-rift sediments
Tectonically thinned transitional crust beneath coastal parts of Gulf Coast basin
Igneous intusive rocks; predominantly Mesozoic granitic rocks. Includes Sierra Nevada batholith, Idaho batholith, and plutons in the North Cascades.

Metamorphic rocks of various metamorphic grads and protoliths. Includes gneiisic and schistose rocks of the North Cascades and in southern Montana, siliciclastic rocks of low metamorphic grade in western Montana and northern Idaho; includes crystalline Mesozoic basement beneath Cretaceous rocks of the Great Valley, including ophiolitic oceanic crust tectonically juxtaposed against Sierran basement rocks to the east, or crystalline rocks underlying Franciscan rocks of the Coast Ranges
Basement type unclassified. Includes highly deformed rocks and structurally intermingled rocks of various types, typically with some igneous or metamorphic component.

Top of bedrock is top of "geophysical basement" as modeled from an iterative inversion of measured gravity data. Gravity data are reduced to Isostatic gravity anomalies using terrain and isostatic gravity corrections. Then the gravity field is numerically separated into two compents: the field caused by higher-density consolidated rocks and the field caused by overlying less dense deposits. Mathematical inversion of basin gravity field yields an estimate of the depth to underlying dense, consolidated rocks. The density of consolidatedt rocks is allowed to vary horizontally, whereas the density of basin-filling deposits increases with depth according to the density-depth relationships constrained with a density-depth function derived from mapped geology and drill-hole information.  In the simplest geologic case in the Basin and Range where unconsolidated basin-fill alluvium overlies consolidated pre-Cenozoic rocks, the method can effectively estimare the depth to the pre-Cenozoic bedrock. Generally, density variations in the basin fill deposits, and in particular the presence of Oligocene and Micoene volcanic rocks with variable density, lead to uncertainty in the geologic identity of the gravity-derived "depth-to-basement" surface.

Top of bedrock is geologically defined as stratified pre-Cenozoic rocks that are represented on "bedrock" geologic maps where Quaternary cover has been removed. Elevation of the top of bedrock is defined by the thickness of overlying Quaternary glacial sediments.

Top of bedrock is geologically defined as stratified pre-Cenozoic rocks that are represented on "bedrock" geologic maps where Quaternary cover has been removed. Elevation of the top of bedrock is defined by the thickness of non-glacial Quaternary alluvium, colluvium, and other unconsolidated deposits, as estimated by surficial geologic maps.

Top of bedrock is geologically defined as the mapped elevation of the base of the Cenozoic section; often the top of Cretaceous rocks. Elevation of the top of bedrock is defined from borehole intercepts, structure contour maps, or surfaces derived from 3D geological modeling.

Bedrock consolidated rock units have been removed by erosion; underlying crystalline basement rocks are exposed at land surface or subcrop beneath Quaternary cover.  Elevation of the top of bedrock is assigned a NULL value
Top of bedrock, as compiled by Shah and others (2018), primarily derived from regional maps and models of sediment thickness, combined with gravity based basin depth maps.
